caveats: Requires two threads to share one Timer instance and call its entry methods (or ensure_started) concurrently while the timer thread is not yet started (deployment model UNCONFIRMED).
The RuntimeError raised by the loser's second start() is threading.Thread stdlib behaviour, outside the tree.
subclaims.reason: Two threads calling entry methods on one Timer (e.g. worker consumer threads via consumer.timer.call_at at T10/celery/worker/strategy.py:119, or Polaroid.install via timer.call_repeatedly at T10/celery/events/snapshot.py:46) both enter _do_enter, which calls ensure_started at T10/celery/utils/timer2.py:117 before taking self.mutex at T10/celery/utils/timer2.py:118. Both can pass the unlocked check at T10/celery/utils/timer2.py:111, since running is a plain attribute set True only inside run() at T10/celery/utils/timer2.py:81 and is_alive() is False until start(). Both then call self.start() at T10/celery/utils/timer2.py:114, and the loser's start() raises RuntimeError because a Thread cannot be started twice. No common lock guards the check-then-act, and no happens-before ordering (no lock, event, or join between the check and start) rules the interleaving out. The window spans many bytecodes and calls including is_alive(), so a GIL switch between bytecodes suffices and no intra-bytecode switch is needed.
